extracted.intended_audience: general readers and natural philosophers skeptical about design; readers of natural theology/early modern physiology
extracted.subtask_description: Use anatomical observations (membranes, vessels, muscles, tendons, joints) and mechanical reasoning to argue for purposive design and infer a wise Creator; the page collects specific structural features as evidences. It combines descriptive anatomy with mechanical/mathematical explanation to persuade skeptics.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Flexibility of the Membranes
rubrics_metrics.description: Membranes and vessels (arteries, veins, nerves, lymphatics) are formed to be flexible so blood and nervous juice can be carried to all parts while joints bend and inflect; their flexible construction is presented as evidence of wise contrivance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation emphasizes that tubes must serve both as receptacles and be able to protrude their contents; the author asks readers to reflect whether such adaptation could arise from 'uncertain and ignorant Causes' rather than 'the greatest Artificer.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex disposition of glands, membranes, ligaments and coverings
rubrics_metrics.description: The existence and arrangement of glands, membranes, ligaments, fat, skin, and cuticula are cited collectively as providing 'Cause enough to extol the Wisdom and Goodness of the Creator.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author treats the catalogue of complementary parts as cumulative evidence; readers are urged to examine discovered anatomical facts and infer design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muscle structure: fibres, belly and tendons
rubrics_metrics.description: A muscle 'consists of a Number of fleshly Fibre or Threads...fastened Top and Bottom to a tough Body, called a Tendon' with transverse fibres interwoven; this architecture explains how contraction draws one tendon to another and produces joint motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anatomical description is used as an evaluative criterion: the precise arrangement (head/tendon fixed, tail/tendon movable, belly composed of fibres) is taken as evidence of purposeful design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of muscles depends on the number of fibres
rubrics_metrics.description: The more fibres in the belly of a muscle that contract, the stronger the muscle's action; this proportional relation is asserted as an observed mechanical law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to infer design: nature arranges many fibres in a limited space to increase force, which the author argues could not be accidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doubling/pennation of muscles to increase force without bulk
rubrics_metrics.description: Muscles arranged obliquely or in doubled rows (figs. 2 and 3) allow many more fibres to act within the same space, producing greater force without excessive thickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author explains several geometric/arrangement variants (oblique insertion, multiple tendinous branches) as ingenious solutions to mechanical problems; these arrangements are presented as criteria for inferring contrivance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of muscle bellies away from delicate structures (e.g., hand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large muscles that require many fibres are placed higher (e.g., in the forearm) with long tendons passing to distal joints so the hand remains thin and dexterous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This spatial planning—locating bulky contractile tissue away from parts needing fine manipulation—is used as an argument for intentional, adaptive design rather than chance placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendons sheaths, bands, and 'door' structures preventing dislocation and disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendons that pass to finger joints are enclosed in membranous sheaths and restrained by bands near the wrist so they do not recede or become disordered during motion; some tendons pass through openings that act like 'a Thread through the Eye of a Needle.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These protective and organizing structures are evaluated as deliberate mechanical solutions to prevent stretching of skin, keep tendons fast to bones, and avoid entanglement—taken as signs of wisdom in design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertion of tendons near bone eminences (pulley-like arrangement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendons are often inserted near knobs/eminences of bones so they act like a rope on a pulley; this keeps the length nearly constant and yields uniform force during contraction, avoids large skin triangles, and reduces the required contraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author uses mechanical reasoning (pulley analogy, arms of levers, obliquity) to show that insertion close to joints preserves form and function—presented as a key design criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint shapes matched to their motions (spherical protuberances and cavities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain joints are formed by a spherical protuberance adapted exactly to a corresponding cavity so the bone can move up/down and side-to-side as appropriate (examples: shoulder, hip, elbow, knee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The precise geometry of joints and their fulfillment of multiple motion requirements is used as evidence of deliberate mechanical design rather than accidental formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mechanical/mathematical principles to evaluate biological function
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanical concepts (levers, arms, obliquity, pulleys, arcs, velocity relations) and mathematical demonstrations (reference to Borelli) are invoked to quantify muscle force and show that anatomical arrangements optimize force and motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author stresses that appealing to mathematics and mechanics strengthens the inference to design; numerical estimates of forces (from Borelli) are given to support awe at the power and contrivance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of opposing muscles preserves symmetry and proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposing muscles maintain parts (e.g., the mouth) in exact middle positions; disease weakening one muscle produces asymmetry, showing that the balanced arrangement is functional and deliberate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symmetry and reciprocal balance are presented as evaluative signs of purposeful arrangement for maintaining proportion and function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude of muscular forces as evidence of extraordinary contrivance
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative examples (e.g., temporalis force, deltoid forces, Glutei exertions, heart force per pulse, and total muscular force during a jump) are cited to show that such great forces produced by 'tender Threads' are astonishing and indicative of design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical claims are used rhetorically to impress readers and to argue that the observed capacities could not arise from 'ignorant Causes'; readers are referred to Borelli for detailed demonstrations.
